result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers confirm the plotted values are correct, but both wrongly call 'about a quarter' misleading even though 27% is about a quarter. Answer A is shorter and its points are more grounded: the missing July to September data is a real gap, since it is now October. Answer B lists more changes, including a comparison line, a y-axis label and a desc element, which pads the review, though B does a better job of saying what to keep. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers wrongly call 'about a quarter' imprecise even though 27% fits that phrase. Both also make the reasonable point that January to June spans five months of change, not six. B is better: it says up front that the chart is accurate, makes fewer and lighter suggestions, and raises a timely question about why the data stops at June when the date is October. A gives a longer list that includes a comparison line from last year, labels on every point and a y-axis label, though it ends by naming what to keep.
